title: Outcome-free sibling-family transfer panel qualification
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Fixed moving-reference and half-rate sibling endpoints provide a bounded transfer panel distinct from retained current training-pool boundaries.
material_change: Hash and compare actual candidate tensors against all sixteen trial-boundary model and pool snapshots plus recorded external-source hashes; CPU load only, zero poker.
notes: Four candidates chosen by family and both seeds before new outcomes. Limited disjointness claim: no certification of discarded intermediate weights or lifetime non-exposure.

result.summary: Four outcome-independently chosen sibling-family candidates passed finite-weight CPU loading and tensor disjointness against80 retained boundary pool snapshots plus16 hero boundaries and known external-source hashes.
result.conclusion: Candidates are distinct from observed current pool boundaries, not certified lifetime unseen opponents. Two related training families with shared ancestry cannot establish universal diversity; no new strength result or poker hands.
result.decision: Use bounded sibling-family transfer panel, not a claim of wholly unseen generalization. Keep Standard10 preservation separate and compare all four retained endpoints against own parents.
result.next_step: Freeze1024 pairs per each of five anchors, two seeds and both control/mixture endpoints:81920 internal executions. Qualify forward compatibility, fresh deck exclusion and controller accounting before launch; no Slumbot.
